---
title: Canonicalization
---

The signature covers the instruction after a named transformation, so the same instruction
verifies whether it arrived through a file, a chat client or an email. The rule is named in the
signed `canon` header field. A verifier applies exactly that rule and never guesses, which is what
stops an attacker from relabelling a block to a rule under which an altered text collapses onto
the signed form.


## Rule Registry

| Rule | Status | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `text/1` | normative | Prose instructions carried through chat, email and Markdown. |
| `raw/1` | normative | Text whose line structure matters. No transport tolerance. |
| `json/1` | reserved (Phase 3) | RFC 8785 over the parsed JSON value. Structured authorizations. |

A rule MUST NOT change once published. A revised rule is a new entry with the next version
suffix (`text/2`). A verifier MAY implement several versions side by side.


## text/1

Input: the instruction segment as a Unicode string. Output: a Unicode string.

1. Apply Unicode Normalization Form C.

2. Replace or remove each character in the fold table below.

3. Split the string on runs of Unicode whitespace, as defined by the `White_Space` property, and
   join the parts with a single U+0020. This collapses every run of spaces, tabs and line breaks
   to one space and removes leading and trailing whitespace.

Fold table:

| Code point | Character | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| U+2018 | left single quotation mark | U+0027 apostrophe |
| U+2019 | right single quotation mark | U+0027 |
| U+201A | single low-9 quotation mark | U+0027 |
| U+201B | single high-reversed-9 quotation mark | U+0027 |
| U+201C | left double quotation mark | U+0022 quotation mark |
| U+201D | right double quotation mark | U+0022 |
| U+201E | double low-9 quotation mark | U+0022 |
| U+201F | double high-reversed-9 quotation mark | U+0022 |
| U+00A0 | no-break space | U+0020 space |
| U+2007 | figure space | U+0020 |
| U+202F | narrow no-break space | U+0020 |
| U+200B | zero width space | removed |
| U+200C | zero width non-joiner | removed |
| U+200D | zero width joiner | removed |
| U+FEFF | zero width no-break space | removed |

`text/1` does not sign line structure. Two instructions that differ only in line breaks, spacing
or typographic quotes have the same canonical form. Two instructions that differ in any other
character do not.


## raw/1

1. Apply Unicode Normalization Form C.

Nothing else. Line endings, indentation and quotes are signed as written. A block under `raw/1`
does not survive re-wrapping by a mail client.


## json/1 (Reserved)

Reserved for Phase 3. Definition: parse the instruction segment as JSON; if it does not parse,
the block is `malformed`; otherwise serialize the value with RFC 8785. Whitespace inside strings
is preserved, key order and number formatting are not signed.


## Requirements

Signers

- A signer MUST apply the rule named in `canon` to the instruction before computing the signing
  input.

- A signer MUST show the signer the canonical form of the instruction, together with `iss`,
  `exp`, `aud` and `canon`, before the signing key is used. The text the human approves is the
  canonical text, not the text as typed.

- A signer SHOULD default to `text/1` for prose.

Verifiers

- A verifier MUST apply only the rule named in `canon`.
- A verifier MUST NOT retry verification under another rule when the first fails.
- A verifier MUST report `malformed` for a rule it does not implement.
- A verifier MUST report the canonical text in the manifest, since that is what was signed.

Adding a rule

- A proposal for a new rule MUST include a collision analysis: which distinct inputs map to the
  same canonical form, and an argument that no such pair differs in meaning for the kind of
  content the rule is for.

- A proposal MUST include test vectors for the rule, including inputs that differ only by the
  transformations the rule is meant to absorb.
